indication: ** 68-year-old male presenting with acute onset non-traumatic left leg pain. Evaluate for arterial occlusion.
technique: ** Helical CT imaging was performed from the level of the aortic bifurcation to the ankles following the intravenous administration of iodinated contrast material. Bolus tracking was utilized to optimize arterial opacification. Multiplanar reformats were reviewed.
findings:
**
The abdominal aorta is widely patent at its bifurcation without evidence of aneurysm. The right common iliac and external iliac arteries demonstrate normal caliber and opacification throughout their course. On the left side, the common and external iliac arteries are patent, showing only mild, non-obstructive atherosclerotic wall thickening.
Regarding the right lower extremity, the common femoral, superficial femoral, and popliteal arteries are patent with no hemodynamically significant stenosis. The trifurcation into the anterior tibial, posterior tibial, and peroneal arteries is preserved.
In the left lower extremity, there is an abrupt termination of contrast opacification arising from the distal aspect of the common femoral artery. This represents an extensive arterial thrombosis extending distally through the entire length of the superficial femoral artery and into the popliteal artery. There is a complete lack of flow in the infrapopliteal runoff vessels, including the anterior and posterior tibial arteries. The deep femoral artery remains patent.
Incidental findings include mild degenerative changes of the hip joints bilaterally, characterized by small marginal osteophytes. There is also a small, stable-appearing simple cyst within the left proximal femur. The visualized musculature of both thighs and calves appears symmetric without evidence of compartment syndrome or significant edema.
conclusion:
**
Extensive arterial thrombosis of the left lower limb originating at the distal common femoral artery and extending distally. No evidence of distal reconstitution.
